children.translated_text: From the affliction of the threefold suffering arises the desire to know the means of removing it.
If [it is said] that [this inquiry] is useless because [remedies] are seen [in the world], [we say] not so, because [such remedies] are not absolute and final.

children.text: 1 abhi M, G(A, D, G); ava J, S
dṛṣṭavad ānuśravikaḥ sa hy a-viśuddhi1 kṣayā'tiśaya-yuktaḥ
children.translated_text: The [remedy] based on scripture (<s>ānuśravika</s>) is like that which is perceived, for it too is connected with impurity, decay, and excess.
Superior to both is [the knowledge] that arises from the discrimination of the manifest (<s>vyakta</s>), the unmanifest (<s>avyakta</s>), and the knower (<s>jña</s>).
The root <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature) is not a modification; the seven [principles] beginning with <s>Mahat</s> are both sources of modification and modifications [themselves].

children.text: ṣoḍaśakas tu vikāro na prakṛtir na vikṛtiḥ puruṣaḥ.
children.translated_text: The group of sixteen are modifications only; <s>Puruṣa</s> (consciousness/spirit) is neither a source of modification nor a modification.
Perception (<s>dṛṣṭa</s>), inference (<s>anumāna</s>), and reliable testimony (<s>āpta-vacana</s>) — because [all] the means of valid knowledge are established [through these three],

children.text: tri-vidhaṃ pramāṇam iṣṭaṃ prameya-siddhiḥ pramāṇād dhi.
children.translated_text: The threefold means of valid knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>) is accepted, for the establishment of what is to be known is indeed from the means of valid knowledge.
Perception is the ascertainment of particular objects. Inference, which is declared to be threefold,
Is preceded by a mark (<s>liṅga</s>) and that which bears the mark (<s>liṅgin</s>). Reliable testimony (<s>āpta-vacana</s>) is the teaching of a reliable person.

children.text: 1 dvi V2 2 liṅgi-liṅga K 3 ca V2, V1, J
sāmānyatas tu dṛṣṭād atī'ndriyāṇām pratītir1 anumānāt
children.translated_text: The cognition of supersensible things is from inference based on general observation (<s>sāmānyato dṛṣṭa</s>).

children.text: tasmād api cā '-siddham paro.akṣam āptā`gamāt siddham2.
children.translated_text: And even what is not established by that [inference] — being beyond the senses — is established by reliable scripture (<s>āptāgama</s>).

children.text: 1 prasiddhir V2, V1, G(D), Y 2 sādhyam Y, M

children.translated_text: [Non-perception may be] due to excessive distance, excessive proximity, damage to the sense organs, instability of the mind,
Subtlety, intervening obstruction, suppression [by something stronger], and intermixture with what is similar.
The non-perception of that [<s>Prakṛti</s>] is due to its subtlety, not to its non-existence; its apprehension is through its effects.

children.text: mahad-ādi tac ca2 kāryam prakṛti-vi-rūpaṃ sa-rūpaṃ3 ca.
children.translated_text: And that effect, beginning with <s>Mahat</s>, is both different from and similar to <s>Prakṛti</s>.

children.text: 1 upalabdheḥ J, V, K 2 tac ca mahad-ādi D
3 sarūpaṃ virūpaṃ J, V; virūpaṃ svarūpaṃ G (G)

children.translated_text: Because the non-existent cannot be produced, because [every effect] requires a material cause (<s>upādāna</s>), because not everything can arise from everything,
Because what is capable can only produce what it is capable of, and because of the nature of the cause — [therefore] the effect pre-exists [in the cause] (<s>sat-kārya</s>).

children.text: hetumad a-nityam a-vyāpi sa-kriyam an-ekam āśritaṃ liṅgam
children.translated_text: The manifest (<s>vyakta</s>) has a cause, is non-eternal, is non-pervasive, is active, is manifold, is dependent, is a mark [of inference],
Has parts, and is subordinate. The unmanifest (<s>avyakta</s>) is the opposite [of all these].

children.text: tri-guṇam a-viveki viṣayaḥ sāmānyam a-cetanaṃ prasava-dharmi
children.translated_text: [Both the manifest and the unmanifest are] possessed of the three <s>guṇas</s>, undiscriminating, objective, common, non-conscious, and productive.

children.text: vyaktaṃ tathā pradhānaṃ tad-viparītas tathā ca pumān.
children.translated_text: The manifest is thus, and so is <s>Pradhāna</s> (the primary cause). <s>Puruṣa</s> is the opposite of these.
[The three <s>guṇas</s>] have the nature of pleasure, displeasure, and torpor; they serve the purposes of illumination, activity, and restraint.
And the <s>guṇas</s> function through mutual dominance, dependence, production, and cooperation.

children.text: sattvaṃ laghu prakāśakam1 iṣṭam upaṣṭambhakaṃ2 calaṃ ca rajaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Sattva</s> is light and illuminating; <s>Rajas</s> is stimulating and mobile;

children.text: guru varaṇakam eva tamaḥ pradīpavac cā 'rthato vṛttiḥ.
children.translated_text: <s>Tamas</s> is heavy and enveloping. Their functioning is for a purpose, like a lamp.

The [nature of <s>Prakṛti</s> as] undiscriminating and so forth is established because of the three-<s>guṇa</s> nature [of effects], and because the opposite [qualities of <s>Puruṣa</s>] are absent [in it].
Because the effect has the nature of the <s>guṇas</s> of its cause, the unmanifest (<s>avyakta</s>) is also established.

children.text: 1 [my emendation]; -ādi-siddhas V1, V2; -ādiḥ siddhas G, J, Y, M;
-ādeḥ siddhis V, D, S; -ādir hi siddhaṃ K 2 viparyaye V
bhedānāṃ parimāṇāt samanvayāc chaktitaḥ pravṛtteś ca
children.translated_text: Because of the finitude of [individual] diversities, because of homogeneity [of similar things], because [the world] proceeds from a potency,
Because of the separation of cause and effect, and because of the non-distinction [at dissolution] of the universal form —

children.text: 1 rūpyasya J, Y, M, V, K
kāraṇam asty avyaktaṃ pravartate tri-guṇataḥ samudayāc1 ca
children.translated_text: There exists the unmanifest (<s>avyakta</s>) as a cause. It operates by means of the three <s>guṇas</s> and through their combination,
Through transformation, like water, due to the specific predominance of each <s>guṇa</s> in turn.
Because a composite serves another's purpose, because [<s>Puruṣa</s>] is the opposite of the three <s>guṇas</s> and the rest, because there must be a controller,
<s>Puruṣa</s> exists — because there must be an experiencer (<s>bhoktṛ</s>), and because [all] activity is for the sake of liberation (<s>kaivalya</s>).
Because of the assigned distribution of birth, death, and faculties, because of [their] non-simultaneous activity,
The plurality of <s>Puruṣas</s> is established, and also because [each is] the opposite of the three <s>guṇas</s>.

children.text: 1 janma V2, V1, G(B, D), M, V, K, D 2 tri-guṇā`di V2, V1, Y
tasmāc ca viparyāsāt1 siddhaṃ sākṣitvam asya puruṣasya
children.translated_text: And from that contrast [with <s>Prakṛti</s>], the witness-nature (<s>sākṣitva</s>) of this <s>Puruṣa</s> is established,
As well as [its] isolation (<s>kaivalya</s>), neutrality (<s>mādhyasthya</s>), seer-nature (<s>draṣṭṛtva</s>), and non-agency (<s>akartṛ-bhāva</s>).

children.text: 1 viparyayāt V1 2 draṣṭitvam V2; praṣṭhitvam V1 3 -bhāvāc V2
tasmāt tat-saṃyogād a-cetanaṃ cetanāvad iva liṅgaṃ
children.translated_text: Therefore, from that conjunction [of <s>Puruṣa</s> and <s>Prakṛti</s>], the non-conscious [<s>Prakṛti</s>] appears as if conscious in the form of the subtle body (<s>liṅga</s>),

children.text: guṇa-1kartṛtve ca2 tathā kart^ eva bhavaty3 udāsīnaḥ4.
children.translated_text: And similarly, though the <s>guṇas</s> are the [real] agents, the indifferent [<s>Puruṣa</s>] appears as if it were the agent.

children.text: 1 guṇāḥ V2 2 .api J, M, V 3 bhavatīty G (note) 4 udāsīnā V2

children.translated_text: For the sake of <s>Puruṣa</s>'s seeing, and likewise for the sake of <s>Pradhāna</s>'s liberation (<s>kaivalya</s>),

children.text: paṅgv-andhavad ubhayor api saṃyogas tat-kṛtaḥ sargaḥ.
children.translated_text: Like [the cooperation of] a lame man and a blind man, there is the conjunction of the two; from that, creation proceeds.

children.text: prakṛter mahāṃs, tato .ahaṃ- kāras, tasmād gaṇaś ca1 ṣoḍaśakaḥ
children.translated_text: From <s>Prakṛti</s> [arises] <s>Mahat</s> (the Great Principle); from that, <s>Ahaṃkāra</s> (the I-principle); and from that, the group of sixteen;

children.text: tasmād api ṣoḍaśakāt pañcabhyaḥ pañca bhūtāni.
children.translated_text: And from five of those sixteen, the five gross elements (<s>bhūtas</s>) arise.

children.text: adhyavasāyo buddhir dharmo jñānaṃ vi-rāga aiśvaryam
children.translated_text: <s>Buddhi</s> (intellect) is determination. <s>Dharma</s> (virtue), knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>), dispassion (<s>virāga</s>), and sovereignty (<s>aiśvarya</s>)
Are its <s>sāttvika</s> (pure) form; the <s>tāmasa</s> (dark) form is the opposite of these.
<s>Ahaṃkāra</s> (the I-principle) is self-conceit. From it proceeds a twofold creation:

children.text: ekādaśakaś ca gaṇas1 tan-mātraḥ2 pañcakaś3 c' aiva.
children.translated_text: The group of eleven and the five <s>tanmātras</s> (subtle elements).

children.text: 1 aindriya ekādaśakas V1, G(B), Y, M
2 mātra- J, M, V, K, S; mātrakaḥ V1 3 pañcakañ S

children.translated_text: The <s>sāttvika</s> group of eleven proceeds from the modified (<s>vaikṛta</s>) <s>Ahaṃkāra</s>;

children.text: bhūtā`des tan1-mātraḥ sa tāmasas taijasād ubhayaṃ.
children.translated_text: The <s>tanmātras</s> proceed from the elemental (<s>bhūtādi</s>) [<s>Ahaṃkāra</s>], which is <s>tāmasa</s>; from the <s>taijasa</s> (fiery) [<s>Ahaṃkāra</s>], both [proceed].
The cognitive sense organs (<s>buddhīndriyāṇi</s>) are called eye, ear, nose, tongue, and skin.
Voice, hands, feet, anus, and genitals are called the organs of action (<s>karmendriyāṇi</s>).

children.text: 1 śrotra- V1, M; karṇa- Y, M (var)
3 sparśanāni V2; sparśanakāni G 4 'pasthāḥ V2, Y;'pasthaṃ K
ubhayā`tmakam atra manaḥ saṃkalpakam indriyaṃ ca sā-dharmyāt
children.translated_text: <s>Manas</s> (mind), being of the nature of both [cognitive and active organs], is deliberative; it is [classified as] a sense organ because of its similarity [to the senses].
The diversity [of things] is due to the specific modifications of the <s>guṇas</s> and to external differences.

children.text: 1 saṃkalpakam atra manaḥ, tac c' endriyam ubhayathā samākhyātam
antas tri-kāla-viṣayaṃ tasmād ubhaya-pracāraṃ tat. V2, Y
2 grāhya M 3 bhedāś G(A, E, F), J, V, S, D

children.translated_text: The function of the five [cognitive organs] with regard to sound and the rest is mere apprehension.
And [the functions] of the five [active organs] are speaking, grasping, locomotion, excretion, and pleasure.

children.text: 1 rūpā`diṣu V2, V1, G(B, D) Y, V 2 -s tu V2, V1, M
children.translated_text: [Variant readings: 'with regard to form and the rest' (V2, V1, G(B, D), Y, V); 'but' (V2, V1, M)]

children.text: svā-lakṣaṇyaṃ1 vṛttis trayasya s^ aiṣā bhavaty a-sāmānyā
children.translated_text: The function of each of the three [internal organs] is its own distinctive [operation]; that is their uncommon [function].
The common function of [all] the organs is the five vital airs (<s>vāyus</s>) beginning with <s>prāṇa</s>.

children.text: yugapac catuṣṭayasya tu1 vṛttiḥ kramaśaś ca tasya nirdiṣṭā
children.translated_text: The function of the four [external and internal organs together] is declared to be [sometimes] simultaneous and [sometimes] successive.

children.text: dṛṣṭe tathā ^py a-dṛṣṭe trayasya tat-pūrvikā vṛttiḥ.
children.translated_text: In both the perceptible (<s>dṛṣṭa</s>) and the imperceptible (<s>adṛṣṭa</s>), the function of the three [internal organs] is preceded by that [of the external organs].
[The organs] perform their respective functions, prompted by each other's impulse.

children.text: puruṣā'rtha eva hetur na kena cit kāryate karaṇam.
children.translated_text: The motive [of the organs] is the purpose of <s>Puruṣa</s> alone; no instrument is activated by anyone [else].

children.text: 1 haitukīṃ K, J; hetukīṃ V1(comm); hetukī Y

children.translated_text: The instrument (<s>karaṇa</s>) is of thirteen kinds; it effects acquisition, retention, and illumination.

children.text: kāryaṃ ca tasya daśadhā *hāryaṃ, dhāryam prakāśyaṃ ca.
children.translated_text: And its object is tenfold — that which is to be acquired, that which is to be retained, and that which is to be illuminated.

children.text: antaḥ-karaṇaṃ tri-vidhaṃ daśadhā bāhyaṃ trayasya viṣayā`khyam
children.translated_text: The internal organ (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>) is threefold; the external is tenfold. These are known as the domain of the three [internal organs].
The external [organs] function only in the present time; the internal organ functions in the three times [past, present, and future].
Of these, the five cognitive sense organs have both specific and non-specific objects.

children.text: vāg bhavati śabda-viṣayā śeṣāṇi tu2 pañca-viṣayāṇi1.
children.translated_text: Speech has sound alone as its object; the remaining [four active organs] have [all] five objects.

children.text: 1 viṣayīṇi V1, J 2 śeṣāṇy api V2, V1, Y, M
sā'ntaḥ-karaṇā buddhiḥ sarvaṃ viṣayam avagāhate yasmāt
children.translated_text: Because <s>Buddhi</s> (intellect), together with the internal organ, apprehends every object,

children.text: tasmāt tri-vidhaṃ karaṇaṃ dvāri dvārāṇi śeṣāṇi.
children.translated_text: Therefore, the threefold [internal] organ is the gatekeeper, and the remaining [ten external organs] are the gates.
These [organs], like lamps, being mutually distinct, being specific modifications of the <s>guṇas</s>,
Having illuminated the entire purpose of <s>Puruṣa</s>, present [it all] to <s>Buddhi</s> (intellect).

children.text: sarvam pratyupabhogaṃ yasmāt puruṣasya sādhayati buddhiḥ
children.translated_text: Because <s>Buddhi</s> accomplishes every experience for <s>Puruṣa</s>,

children.text: s^ aiva ca viśinaṣṭi punaḥ1 pradhāna-puruṣā'ntaraṃ sūkṣmam.
children.translated_text: She alone also discriminates the subtle difference between <s>Pradhāna</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s>.

children.text: tan-mātrāṇy a-viśeṣās tebhyo bhūtāni pañca pañcabhyaḥ
children.translated_text: The <s>tanmātras</s> (subtle elements) are non-specific (<s>aviśeṣa</s>); from them arise the five gross elements from the five [<s>tanmātras</s>].

children.text: ete smṛtā viśeṣāḥ śāntā ghorāś ca mūḍhāś ca1.
children.translated_text: These [gross elements] are considered specific (<s>viśeṣa</s>); they are calm (<s>śānta</s>), violent (<s>ghora</s>), and dull (<s>mūḍha</s>).

children.text: 1 santo [śānto ?] ghoraś ca mūḍhaś ca V1
sūkṣmā mātā-pitṛ-jāḥ saha prabhūtais tridhā viśeṣāḥ syuḥ
children.translated_text: The subtle, the born-from-parents, and together with the gross — thus the specific [bodies] are of three kinds.
Of these, the subtle [bodies] are permanent; the bodies born from parents perish.
Arising before [the gross body], unattached, permanent, consisting of [the principles] from <s>Mahat</s> down to the subtle elements —
The subtle body (<s>liṅga</s>), without [independent] enjoyment, perfumed by dispositions (<s>bhāvas</s>), transmigrates.

children.text: citraṃ yathā *śrayam ṛte sthāṇv1-ādibhyo vinā yathā2 chāyā
children.translated_text: Just as a picture [does not stand] without a support, just as a shadow [does not exist] without a post and the like,

children.text: tadvad vinā ^viśeṣair na tiṣṭhati3 nir-āśrayaṃ liṅgam.
children.translated_text: So too, without the non-specific [subtle elements], the subtle body does not stand, being without support.

children.text: 1 tantv K 2 yathā vinā G, D 3 -s tiṣṭhati na M

children.translated_text: This [subtle body], motivated by the purpose of <s>Puruṣa</s>, by the connection of cause and effect,
The subtle body, by virtue of the versatile power of <s>Prakṛti</s>, performs [its roles] like a dancer.

children.text: sāṃsiddhikāś ca bhāvāḥ prākṛtikā vaikṛtāś ca dharmā`dyāḥ
children.translated_text: The dispositions (<s>bhāvas</s>), beginning with <s>dharma</s> (virtue) and the rest, are innate (<s>sāṃsiddhika</s>), natural (<s>prākṛtika</s>), and acquired (<s>vaikṛta</s>).
They are seen to depend on the instruments [i.e., internal organs]; and those depending on the effects [i.e., bodies] are the embryo (<s>kalala</s>) and the rest.

children.text: dharmeṇa gamanam ūrdhvaṃ gamanam adhastād bhavaty a-dharmeṇa
children.translated_text: By virtue (<s>dharma</s>), there is movement upward; by vice (<s>adharma</s>), there is movement downward.
By knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>), there is liberation (<s>apavarga</s>); from its opposite [ignorance], bondage is held [to result].

children.text: vai-rāgyāt prakṛti-layaḥ saṃsāro bhavati rājasād1 rāgāt
children.translated_text: From dispassion (<s>vairāgya</s>), [there is] dissolution into <s>Prakṛti</s>; from passionate attachment (<s>rāga</s>), which is <s>rājasa</s>, [there is continued] transmigration (<s>saṃsāra</s>).
From sovereignty (<s>aiśvarya</s>), [there is] non-obstruction; from its opposite, the reverse.
This is the intellectual creation (<s>pratyaya-sarga</s>), called error (<s>viparyaya</s>), incapacity (<s>aśakti</s>), contentment (<s>tuṣṭi</s>), and attainment (<s>siddhi</s>).

children.text: guṇa-vaiṣamya1-vimardāt2 tasya ca3 bhedās tu pañcāśat.
children.translated_text: Due to the disparity and conflict of the <s>guṇas</s>, there are fifty subdivisions of it.

children.text: 1 vaiśamya K 2 vimarśāt T, K; vimardena V2, V1(comm), J, M; vimarde V1
pañca viparyaya-bhedā bhavanty a-śakteś1 ca karaṇa-vaikalyāt
children.translated_text: There are five kinds of error; and incapacity, due to the deficiency of the organs,
Has twenty-eight kinds. Contentment (<s>tuṣṭi</s>) is ninefold; attainment (<s>siddhi</s>) is eightfold.

children.text: 1 a-śaktiś V1, G (except for D), J, Y, V, K 2 bhedā V1, J, Y, M, V, K
bhedas tamaso .aṣṭa-vidho mohasya ca daśa-vidho mahā-mohaḥ
children.translated_text: The division of <s>tamas</s> (darkness) is eightfold; that of <s>moha</s> (delusion) is tenfold; <s>mahāmoha</s> (great delusion)
<s>Tāmisra</s> (gloom) is of eighteen kinds; and similarly, <s>andhatāmisra</s> (blind darkness) [is of eighteen kinds].

children.text: ekādaś' endriya-vadhāḥ1 saha buddhi-vadhair a-śaktir uddiṣṭā2
children.translated_text: Incapacity (<s>aśakti</s>) is stated to be the eleven impairments of the sense organs, together with the impairments of <s>Buddhi</s> —
The seventeen impairments of <s>Buddhi</s>, being the reversals of contentment and attainment.

children.text: 1 vadhā G 2 upadiṣṭā J, K 3 saptadaśa-dhā G; . ca J, K; . tu D
4 buddhir Y 5 viparyayās J; viparyayā K

children.translated_text: The four internal [contentments] are called [those relating to] nature (<s>prakṛti</s>), means (<s>upādāna</s>), time (<s>kāla</s>), and fortune (<s>bhāgya</s>).

children.text: bāhyā viṣay'oparamāc ca pañca3 nava4 tuṣṭayo .abhimatāḥ 5.
children.translated_text: And the five external [contentments] arise from abstention from sense objects. Thus nine contentments are recognized.

children.text: 1 ādhy-ātmikyaś G(E), Y, M; adhy-ātmikāś K 2 bhāga V1, G(F), D
3 -ramāt pañca ca Y, V, K; -ramāt pañca J, M, B, S;
-ramāś ca pañca V1, G(D); -ramāḥ pañca D
4 nava ca M 5 -hitāḥ G(D, F), Y, M, D

children.translated_text: Reasoning (<s>ūha</s>), verbal instruction (<s>śabda</s>), study (<s>adhyayana</s>), the three kinds of removal of suffering, the attainment of friends (<s>suhṛt-prāpti</s>),

children.text: dānaṃ ca siddhayo .aṣṭau2 siddheḥ3 pūrvo .aṅkuśas tri-vidhaḥ
children.translated_text: And generosity (<s>dāna</s>) — these are the eight attainments (<s>siddhis</s>). The threefold impediment precedes attainment.

children.text: 1 -vighāta-trayaṃ V1, M 2 siddha-yogo K 3 siddhi V2; siddhe V1
na vinā bhāvair liṅgaṃ na vinā liṅgena bhāva-1nirvṛttiḥ2
children.translated_text: Without the dispositions (<s>bhāvas</s>), the subtle body [cannot function]; without the subtle body, there is no completion of the dispositions.
Therefore, a twofold creation proceeds — one called the subtle body (<s>liṅga</s>) and one called the dispositions (<s>bhāva</s>).

children.text: 2 vinivṛttiḥ V1; saṃsiddhiḥ Y, M(var.); niṣpattiḥ J, M(var)
aṣṭa-vikalpo daivas1 tairyag-yonaś2 ca3 pañcadhā bhavati
children.translated_text: The divine (<s>daiva</s>) [creation] is eightfold; the animal (<s>tairyag-yona</s>) is fivefold;

children.text: mānuṣyaś4 c' aika5-vidhaḥ samāsato bhautikaḥ6 sargaḥ.
children.translated_text: And the human (<s>mānuṣya</s>) is of one kind — this, in brief, is the elemental (<s>bhautika</s>) creation.

children.text: G(D) [uses neuter in the first three half-lines:
1 devas V1 2 tiryag-yoniś V1; tairyag-yonyaś J 3 [missing] G(D)
4 mānuśakaś V (var) 5 tv eka G(D) 6 .ayaṃ tridhā G(D)
ūrdhvaṃ sattva-viśālas tamo-viśālaś ca1 mūlataḥ sargaḥ
children.translated_text: The creation above [is] predominantly <s>sattva</s>; and that at the base is predominantly <s>tamas</s>.
In the middle it is predominantly <s>rajas</s> — from <s>Brahmā</s> down to a blade of grass.

children.text: 1 -as tu V1, Y, M(var) 2 -iḥ D 3 -aṃ G (comm -aḥ)
tatra1 jarā-maraṇa-kṛtaṃ2 duḥkham prāpnoti cetanaḥ puruṣaḥ
children.translated_text: Therein, the conscious <s>Puruṣa</s> experiences suffering caused by old age and death,
Due to the non-cessation of the <s>liṅga</s> (subtle body), therefore suffering is inherent by nature.

children.text: 1 atra V1, Y, M; atra janma- Y(comm. to verse 1)
2 [missing] V2 3 'pi V1 4 samāsena V1, Y, M

children.translated_text: Thus this creation made by <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature), extending from <s>Mahat</s> (the great principle) down to the specific gross elements,
is undertaken for the liberation of each <s>Puruṣa</s> (consciousness) — seemingly for its own sake, but really for the sake of another.

children.text: 1 kṛtau G(D); kṛtaḥ Y; vikṛtaḥ V1 2 viṣaya M

children.translated_text: Just as the flow of milk, which is insentient, occurs for the purpose of the calf's nourishment,
so too the activity of <s>Pradhāna</s> (the chief principle) is for the purpose of <s>Puruṣa</s>'s liberation.
Just as the world engages in activities for the purpose of relieving anxiety,
so likewise the <s>Avyakta</s> (unmanifest) acts for the purpose of <s>Puruṣa</s>'s liberation.

children.text: raṅgasya darśayitvā nivartate nartakī yathā nṛtyāt
children.translated_text: Just as a dancer retires from the dance after having displayed herself to the audience,
so <s>Prakṛti</s> withdraws after having revealed herself to <s>Puruṣa</s>.
By various means, she who is helpful acts for the unhelpful <s>Puruṣa</s>;

children.text: guṇavaty a-guṇasya satas tasyā 'rtham apā'rthakaṃ carati2.
children.translated_text: she who possesses <s>guṇas</s> (constituents) acts purposelessly for the purpose of that <s>Puruṣa</s> who is without <s>guṇas</s>.

children.text: prakṛteḥ su-kumārataraṃ na kiṃ-cid astī 'ti me matir bhavati
children.translated_text: Nothing is more delicate than <s>Prakṛti</s> — so it is, I think;

children.text: yā dṛṣṭā ^smī 'ti punar na darśanam upaiti puruṣasya.
children.translated_text: she who, thinking "I have been seen," never again comes into the sight of <s>Puruṣa</s>.

children.text: tasmān na badhyate1 .addhā na2 mucyate3 nā 'pi saṃsarati kaś-cit4
children.translated_text: Therefore truly no one is bound, no one is released, nor does anyone transmigrate;

children.text: saṃsarati badhyate mucyate ca nānā*śrayā prakṛtiḥ
children.translated_text: it is <s>Prakṛti</s>, abiding in various substrates, that transmigrates, is bound, and is released.

children.text: 1 mucyate G(C), D 2 nā 'pi G, M, K, D; na V1; [missing] V2
3 badhyate G(C), D; [missing] V2 4 puruṣaḥ B, D, S ; kiṃ-cit V2
rūpaiḥ saptabhir eva tu1 badhnāty ātmānam ātmanā prakṛtiḥ
children.translated_text: By seven forms indeed <s>Prakṛti</s> binds herself by herself;

children.text: s^ aiva ca puruṣā'rtham prati2 vimocayaty ekarūpeṇa.
children.translated_text: and she herself liberates by a single form, for the purpose of <s>Puruṣa</s>.

children.text: 1 evaṃ V1, M; eva V2, G
2 puruṣasyā 'rthaṃ prati M; puruṣasyā 'rthaṃ V2, D
[This verse is missing in Paramārtha's Chinese version (T)]
evaṃ tattvā'bhyāsān nā 'smi na me nā 'ham ity a-pariśeṣam
children.translated_text: Thus, from the contemplation of the <s>tattvas</s> (principles), there arises the knowledge "I am not, nothing is mine, there is no I" — without remainder,
free from error, pure — absolute <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge) arises.
By that knowledge, <s>Puruṣa</s> sees <s>Prakṛti</s>, whose production has ceased, who has withdrawn from the seven forms because her purpose is fulfilled,

children.text: prakṛtim paśyati puruṣaḥ prekṣakavad avasthitaḥ su-sthaḥ2.
children.translated_text: standing firm and well-established, like a spectator.

children.text: 1 vinivṛttaḥ V2, V1 2 sva-sthaḥ V2, V1, J, M, V; svacchaḥ V(var), K
dṛṣṭā may^ ety1 upekṣaka2 eko dṛṣṭā ^ham ity uparatā ^nyā3
children.translated_text: "She has been seen by me," thinks the indifferent one; "I have been seen," the other has ceased —

children.text: sati saṃyoge .api tayoḥ prayojanaṃ ṇā 'sti sargasya.
children.translated_text: even though conjunction of the two persists, there is no motive for further creation.

children.text: 3 uparat^ aikā V2(?),V1, G(D); uparamaty anyā G(var), J(var), V, K, S

children.translated_text: From the attainment of right knowledge, when <s>dharma</s> and the rest cease to be operative causes,
the embodied one continues bearing a body by the force of <s>saṃskāras</s> (latent impressions), like the spinning of a potter's wheel.
When bodily dissolution is reached, and <s>Pradhāna</s> has withdrawn because its purpose is fulfilled,
<s>Puruṣa</s> attains <s>kaivalya</s> (isolation) that is both absolute and final.
This secret knowledge concerning <s>Puruṣa</s>'s purpose was declared by the supreme sage <s>Kapila</s>,
wherein the origination, subsistence, and dissolution of beings are contemplated.

children.translated_text: The sage <s>Kapila</s> gave this pure and supreme teaching to <s>Āsuri</s> out of compassion;

children.text: AAsurir api Pañca-śikhāya tena1 bahudhā2-kṛtaṃ tantram.
children.translated_text: <s>Āsuri</s> likewise transmitted it to <s>Pañcaśikha</s>, by whom the doctrine was expanded in many ways.

abridged by one of noble intellect, having fully understood the established doctrine.

though devoid of illustrative stories and free from polemics against rival doctrines.

like an image reflected in a mirror of the great body of the doctrine.
